analysis.subject: computing
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers common phishing tactics and scam email signs, four ways to protect devices and accounts including multi-factor authentication, and how to report suspected messages.

overview.headline: How to recognize phishing messages and protect your accounts

keyPoints.point: Students learn that scammers use email and text messages to steal passwords and account numbers.
keyPoints.quote: Scammers use email or text messages to try to steal your passwords, account numbers, or Social Security numbers.

keyPoints.point: Phishing emails often report suspicious activity to trick recipients into clicking links.
keyPoints.quote: say they’ve noticed some suspicious activity or log-in attempts — they haven’t

keyPoints.point: A generic greeting and a fake billing problem are signs of a phishing scam email.
keyPoints.quote: The email has a generic greeting.

keyPoints.point: Multi-factor authentication makes it harder for scammers to access accounts even with stolen passwords.
keyPoints.quote: Multi-factor authentication makes it harder for scammers to log in to your accounts if they do get your username and password.

keyTerms.gloss: phishing attacks that use deceptive messages to steal personal information
keyTerms.quote: Scammers launch thousands of phishing attacks like these every day — and they’re often successful.

keyTerms.gloss: authentication requiring two or more credentials to protect accounts
keyTerms.quote: Protect your accounts by using multi-factor authentication.

keyTerms.gloss: malware is harmful software installed when you click a deceptive link
keyTerms.quote: want you to click on a link to make a payment — but the link has malware

keyTerms.gloss: spam filters that help keep phishing emails out of the inbox
keyTerms.quote: Your email spam filters might keep many phishing emails out of your inbox.

keyTerms.gloss: identity theft occurs when scammers use stolen personal information to access accounts
keyTerms.quote: Phishing emails can often have real consequences for people who give scammers their information, including identity theft.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Students apply the ordered protection steps to build layered defenses against phishing attacks.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Here are four ways to protect yourself from phishing attacks.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Learners classify authentication credentials to understand how multi-factor protection blocks account takeover.
componentPlan.focusQuote: The extra credentials you need to log in to your account fall into three categories:
